newsitem.title: CANADA: Loewen drops after analyst downgrades shrs.
newsitem.headline: Loewen drops after analyst downgrades shrs.

text.p: Shares in the Loewen Group Inc fell Thursday after brokerage Alex. Brown lowered its rating on the funeral home company's stock and investors trimmed earnings 1997 forecasts.
Loewen stock dropped 1-1/8 to 32-1/8 in New York and 1.45 to 44 in Toronto.
Alex. Brown analyst Camille Humphries said she downgraded Loewen to a buy, down from strong buy, after the company reported fourth-quarter earnings on Wednesday.
Loewen earned US$0.36 a share in the fourth quarter before after-tax costs of US$0.23 a share related to fighting a hostile takeover bid by Service Corp International.
Humphries said the earnings fell short of her original expectations of US$0.42 a share and she lowered her 1997 earnings estimate to US$1.58 a share from US$1.70.
While Loewen's long-term prospects are bright, the takeover bid, which was dropped in January, and a legal battle that nearly forced the company into bankruptcy last year were distractions, she said.

"It's going to take a quarter or two for them to get back on track," Humphries said. She said she lowered her rating on the stock to allow a few months for "a reacceleration of fundamentals" in anticipation of re-raising it later.
Other analysts said the fourth-quarter results were disappointing, although most had forecast earnings before the takeover costs around US$0.37 to US$0.39.
While the company previously said it was comfortable with 1997 forecasts around US$1.70 a share, some analysts were revising forecasts to around US$1.60 a share.

Loewen said Wednesday that it was comfortable with forecasts of 25 percent EPS growth for 1997. It earned US$1.27 a share in 1996 before costs associated with the takeover, and 25 percent growth from there would translate into earnings of about US$1.59 share.
Loewen spokesman David Laundy said the company was proud of its 1996 performance and optimistic about 1997.

"To report record revenues and earnings for 1996 is an outstanding achievement given the distraction of the failed SCI hostile takeover attempt," he said. "These results validate the strength of our business plan...(and) we can now turn our attention to delivering consistent and superior earnings growth."
